The Data of a Graph

Source: R/plot_core.R
plot_data.Rd

Computes the quantities that a graph draws and returns them as a named list of data frames, one for each layer. It dispatches on the type and on x: the term for a term_plot, the family of the fit for a model_plot or a diagnostic_plot.

Usage

plot_data(type, x, fit, ctx, ...)

Arguments

type

An object inheriting from plot_type.

x

The term or the family on which the method dispatches.

fit

A StatmodFit().

ctx

The context described in the details.

...

Unused.

Value

A named list of data frames.

Details

A method has the signature function(type, x, fit, ctx, ...). The context ctx is a list with the elements param (the equation, or NULL), name (the name of the term in that equation, or NULL), vars (the variables whose effect is drawn), cols (the positions within the term's coefficients that belong to those variables, or NULL for all of them), data (the data frame passed to autoplot.StatmodFit(), or NULL) and title (what term named: the term, or the variable). The list that a method returns may carry the attribute "labels", a list of arguments of ggplot2::labs() (title, x, y and others), which autoplot.StatmodFit() applies to the graph.

See also

plot_layers(), plot_type

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(100))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
str(plot_data(plot_effect(), fit@spec@terms$mu[["s(x)"]], fit,
              ctx = list(param = "mu", name = "s(x)", vars = "x",
                         cols = NULL, data = dd)), max.level = 1)
#> List of 4
#>  $ curve :'data.frame':	200 obs. of  4 variables:
#>  $ points:'data.frame':	100 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ bins  :'data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ rug   :'data.frame':	100 obs. of  1 variable:
#>  - attr(*, "kind")= chr "numeric"
#>  - attr(*, "labels")=List of 5
